name: Ways to combine two signals
title: Fusion: the four ways to combine two signals, and which one the paper picks
blurb: The taught paper holds two descriptions of every vertex — a one-number structural embedding and a many-number rule embedding — and has to combine them into one representation. This section lays out the four standard ways to do that (concatenation, weighted sum, elementwise gating, cross-attention), shows with worked arithmetic what each one gains and what each one loses, and then identifies exactly which one the paper uses: a broadcast gate followed by concatenation.
skip_hint: If you can say what concatenation does to two widths, why a fixed weighted sum pre-commits to a ratio that training cannot undo, and why a one-column gate can only rescale a whole row, skip this section.
